text_blocks.snippet: Infusion drugs are medications administered directly into the bloodstream, often through an intravenous (IV) line. These can include a wide range of medications used to treat various conditions, including infections, autoimmune diseases, and neurological disorders. Some examples include antibiotics, antifungals, and disease-modifying therapies for conditions like multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis.
Common Infusion Drugs and Their Uses:

list.title: Antibiotics:
list.snippet: Used to treat bacterial infections, especially severe ones. Examples include vancomycin, ceftriaxone, and ciprofloxacin.

list.title: Antifungals:
list.snippet: Used to treat fungal infections, often in immunocompromised patients. Examples include amphotericin B, caspofungin, and anidulafungin.
